module_name: Tools Stack: Python, R, and Commercial Platforms Compared
module_description: Module 27 gives parity training: what the open-source stack can do (Python: pandas, transformers, bertopic, networkx/leidenalg, praw/atproto; R: rtweet/tidytext/quanteda/ggraph/stm), what commercial platforms (Brandwatch, Meltwater, Talkwalker, Sprout Social, Pulsar) sell, and where the boundary lies. Students benchmark free vs paid output on one question and learn to justify tool choices - a job-interview and procurement skill.
core_concepts: Python stack for each analytics family (text, network, video)
R stack for text and networks (tidytext, quanteda, igraph, stm)
learning_outcomes: C3 Implement an analysis in both Python and R
C4 Benchmark commercial vs open-source output on the same question
C5 Justify a tool choice for a given scenario
methods_models: Parallel implementation in Python and R, benchmark protocol (same query, same metric, same window)
evaluation_metrics: Output agreement across implementations, runtime, cost of implementation, and qualitative gap analysis
pitfalls_limitations: Assuming vendor metrics equal your computation, opacity of vendor algorithms, licensing constraints, R/Python result differences from library versions
tools_stack: Full Python/R stacks as above, conda/renv, jupyter
tools_access_cost: Commercial platforms are licensed per seat and rarely in university budget; open source is free
lab_activities: Same question analysed in Python and R, and benchmarked against a vendor trial or public demo
assessment_methods: Benchmark report plus a build-vs-buy justification; graded on evidence quality and cost reasoning
data_collection_workflow: Define benchmark question -> collect once -> analyse in both stacks -> compare outputs, runtimes and costs -> document discrepancy sources
textbooks: Silge & Robinson, Text Mining with R (R pipeline)
Wickham & Grolemund, R for Data Science
Official docs of the commercial platforms
key_papers: 2025-2026 vendor documentation and industry comparisons of social-listening tools
trends_2024_2026: 2024-2026: agentic/AI features entered vendor products while open LLM models matured, so build-vs-buy expanded into build-vs-lease-vs-agent
industry_relevance: Industry parity checks: students benchmark free tools against commercial platforms (Pulsar, Talkwalker, Meltwater, Brandwatch, Sprout Social) to learn which metrics the market actually sells, and how to justify a tool purchase.
localization_context: Cost realism for Indonesian labs: most commercial social-listening seats are out of university budget, so the module builds an open-source pipeline and teaches read-only academic access paths that are free.
ethics_regulation: Data licensing and redistribution limits of each tool, platform Terms of Service restrictions on scraping, and storage of raw data with access control; UU PDP requires minimization when datasets contain personal text.
case_study_scenarios: Decide build vs buy for a client's monitoring need and defend it with evidence and cost.
